children: Led by Masayoshi Son, Japanese tech investment firm SoftBank Group Corp. (SFTBY, Financials) is set to repay a $25.9 billion bridge loan ahead of schedule. Repayment size is getting attention. What Son does next could be even more intriguing.

The borrowing is related to SoftBank's investments in OpenAI, and is part of a far bigger effort by Son to put artificial intelligence at the heart of the company's strategy. But paying off the debt early doesn't mean spending is stopping.
For finance, SoftBank might tap its interest in Arm Holdings PLC , the chip designer that has become one of the group's most valuable assets. That provides Son another avenue of financial firepower.
There is risk too. That works well as long as the stock is strong, and you can borrow against Arm shares. And a sharp drop could make for a lot less comfortable of a plan.
That trade-off is huge because SoftBank has never been afraid to make big bets. AI is just the latest, and maybe the biggest.

For investors, this $25.9 billion repayment is not exactly the end of the story. But the most crucial question is what lies beyond it. If Son is making space for another big AI wager, the next deal may reveal more to investors about where SoftBank is headed.

title: SoftBank Just Freed Up $25.9 Billion and Its Next AI Move Could Be Huge
